steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren lit the lamp at dusk, same as she had for thirty-one years.

The storm came fast — the way Atlantic storms always did, without apology. Rain hammered the glass. The sea below turned white and furious.

At midnight, she saw them: a fishing boat, tilting badly, caught between the rocks and the dark.

She turned the light up as high as it would go and watched, hands pressed flat against the cold glass, barely breathing.

The boat turned.

Slowly, painfully, it turned toward open water and safety.

Maren exhaled.

She never knew the names of the people she saved. They never knew hers. That was the whole point, really — to shine without needing to be thanked, to stand in the dark so others didn't have to.

She put the kettle on and waited for morning.
